question: Register the database
sql: SELECT frogql_register_database('social_network_twitter', '/home/maxdemarzi/vsql-frogql/examples/social_network_twitter.gdb')

question: Identify users who have posted tweets containing hashtags that belong to trends with a tweet volume greater than 10000, and return their usernames along with the trend names.
sql: SELECT graph.username, graph.name FROM JSON_TABLE(CONVERT(frogql_traverse('social_network_twitter', 'MATCH (u:USER)-[:POSTS]->(t:TWEET)-[:CONTAINS_HASHTAG]->(h:HASHTAG)-[:BELONGS_TO_TREND]->(tr:TREND) WHERE tr.tweet_volume > 10000 RETURN DISTINCT u.username, tr.name') USING utf8mb4), '$[*]' COLUMNS(username VARCHAR(255) PATH '$[0]', name VARCHAR(255) PATH '$[1]')) AS graph
sql_json: SELECT frogql_traverse('social_network_twitter', 'MATCH (u:USER)-[:POSTS]->(t:TWEET)-[:CONTAINS_HASHTAG]->(h:HASHTAG)-[:BELONGS_TO_TREND]->(tr:TREND) WHERE tr.tweet_volume > 10000 RETURN DISTINCT u.username, tr.name')

question: Identify the top 5 most engaged-with tweets (based on total engagements) posted by users who have more than 100 followers, including details about the tweet content, user display name, and engagement count.
sql: SELECT graph.content, graph.display_name, graph.COUNTDISTINCT FROM JSON_TABLE(CONVERT(frogql_traverse('social_network_twitter', 'MATCH (u:USER)-[:POSTS]->(t:TWEET)<-[e:ENGAGES_WITH]-(:USER) WHERE u.followers_count > 100 GROUP BY t.content, u.display_name RETURN t.content, u.display_name, COUNT(DISTINCT e) ORDER BY COUNT(DISTINCT e) DESC LIMIT 5') USING utf8mb4), '$[*]' COLUMNS(content TEXT PATH '$[0]', display_name VARCHAR(255) PATH '$[1]', COUNTDISTINCT INT PATH '$[2]')) AS graph
sql_json: SELECT frogql_traverse('social_network_twitter', 'MATCH (u:USER)-[:POSTS]->(t:TWEET)<-[e:ENGAGES_WITH]-(:USER) WHERE u.followers_count > 100 GROUP BY t.content, u.display_name RETURN t.content, u.display_name, COUNT(DISTINCT e) ORDER BY COUNT(DISTINCT e) DESC LIMIT 5')

question: Retrieve a list of users who have posted tweets containing media attachments and also belong to at least one list, showing their usernames, the number of lists they're part of, and the count of media attachments in their tweets.
sql: SELECT graph.username, graph.COUNTDISTINCT, graph.COUNTDISTINCT_1 FROM JSON_TABLE(CONVERT(frogql_traverse('social_network_twitter', 'MATCH (u:USER)-[:POSTS]->(t:TWEET)-[:ATTACHES_MEDIA]->(m:MEDIA_ATTACHMENT), (u)-[:MEMBER_OF_LIST]->(l:LIST) GROUP BY u.username RETURN u.username, COUNT(DISTINCT l), COUNT(DISTINCT m)') USING utf8mb4), '$[*]' COLUMNS(username VARCHAR(255) PATH '$[0]', COUNTDISTINCT INT PATH '$[1]', COUNTDISTINCT_1 INT PATH '$[2]')) AS graph

question: Retrieve the average number of likes per tweet for users who have posted more than 10 tweets and whose tweets include media attachments. Include only tweets that are not marked as sensitive.

question: Find the average number of tweets posted per user for users who have engaged with at least 10 tweets organically and have a verified status, excluding users who follow more than 1000 accounts.

sql_json: SELECT frogql_traverse('social_network_twitter', 'MATCH (u:USER{verified_status:true}), (u)-[e:ENGAGES_WITH{is_organic:true}]->(:TWEET), (u)-[:POSTS]->(t:TWEET) WHERE u.following_count <= 1000 RETURN AVG(u.tweet_count) AS average_tweets_per_user')

question: List the usernames of users who have engaged with tweets containing specific hashtags and have also followed at least one other user. Include only those engagements that were organic.
sql: SELECT graph.username FROM JSON_TABLE(CONVERT(frogql_traverse('social_network_twitter', 'MATCH (u:USER)-[e:ENGAGES_WITH]->(t:TWEET)-[:CONTAINS_HASHTAG]->(h:HASHTAG), (u)-[:FOLLOWS]->(:USER) WHERE e.is_organic = true RETURN u.username') USING utf8mb4), '$[*]' COLUMNS(username VARCHAR(255) PATH '$[0]')) AS graph
sql_json: SELECT frogql_traverse('social_network_twitter', 'MATCH (u:USER)-[e:ENGAGES_WITH]->(t:TWEET)-[:CONTAINS_HASHTAG]->(h:HASHTAG), (u)-[:FOLLOWS]->(:USER) WHERE e.is_organic = true RETURN u.username')

sql_json: SELECT frogql_traverse('social_network_twitter', 'MATCH (u:USER)-[:POSTS]->(t:TWEET), (u)-[:MEMBER_OF_LIST]->(:LIST) WHERE t.view_count > 1000 AND u.followers_count > 1000 RETURN u.display_name')

sql_json: SELECT frogql_traverse('social_network_twitter', 'MATCH (tr:TREND) RETURN tr.name, tr.tweet_volume ORDER BY tr.tweet_volume DESC LIMIT 5')

question: Retrieve the list names and member counts for lists created by users who have more than 1000 followers and are verified. Order the results by member count in descending order.
sql: SELECT graph.name, graph.member_count FROM JSON_TABLE(CONVERT(frogql_traverse('social_network_twitter', 'MATCH (u:USER{verified_status:true})-[:MEMBER_OF_LIST]->(l:LIST) WHERE u.followers_count > 1000 RETURN l.name, l.member_count ORDER BY l.member_count DESC') USING utf8mb4), '$[*]' COLUMNS(name VARCHAR(255) PATH '$[0]', member_count INT PATH '$[1]')) AS graph
sql_json: SELECT frogql_traverse('social_network_twitter', 'MATCH (u:USER{verified_status:true})-[:MEMBER_OF_LIST]->(l:LIST) WHERE u.followers_count > 1000 RETURN l.name, l.member_count ORDER BY l.member_count DESC')

question: List the top 10 users with the highest total engagement (sum of likes, retweets, and replies) on their tweets, who have posted at least 5 tweets and are not verified.
sql: SELECT graph.username, graph.like_count FROM JSON_TABLE(CONVERT(frogql_traverse('social_network_twitter', 'MATCH (u:USER)-[:POSTS]->(t:TWEET) WHERE u.verified_status = false GROUP BY u.username RETURN u.username, SUM(t.like_count) ORDER BY SUM(t.like_count) DESC LIMIT 10') USING utf8mb4), '$[*]' COLUMNS(username VARCHAR(255) PATH '$[0]', like_count INT PATH '$[1]')) AS graph
sql_json: SELECT frogql_traverse('social_network_twitter', 'MATCH (u:USER)-[:POSTS]->(t:TWEET) WHERE u.verified_status = false GROUP BY u.username RETURN u.username, SUM(t.like_count) ORDER BY SUM(t.like_count) DESC LIMIT 10')

question: Retrieve the average view count of tweets for each language, considering only tweets that have been retweeted more than 10 times and were posted by users with more than 1000 followers.
sql: SELECT graph.language, graph.avg_view_count FROM JSON_TABLE(CONVERT(frogql_traverse('social_network_twitter', 'MATCH (u:USER)-[:POSTS]->(t:TWEET) WHERE u.followers_count > 1000 AND t.retweet_count > 10 GROUP BY t.language RETURN t.language, AVG(t.view_count) AS avg_view_count ORDER BY avg_view_count DESC') USING utf8mb4), '$[*]' COLUMNS(language INT PATH '$[0]', avg_view_count DOUBLE PATH '$[1]')) AS graph
sql_json: SELECT frogql_traverse('social_network_twitter', 'MATCH (u:USER)-[:POSTS]->(t:TWEET) WHERE u.followers_count > 1000 AND t.retweet_count > 10 GROUP BY t.language RETURN t.language, AVG(t.view_count) AS avg_view_count ORDER BY avg_view_count DESC')

question: List the names of trends along with the number of hashtags associated with each trend, for trends that have at least one hashtag ranked in the top 5 positions.
sql: SELECT graph.name, graph.hashtag_count FROM JSON_TABLE(CONVERT(frogql_traverse('social_network_twitter', 'MATCH (h:HASHTAG)-[b:BELONGS_TO_TREND]->(tr:TREND) WHERE b.rank_position <= 5 GROUP BY tr.name RETURN tr.name, COUNT(h) AS hashtag_count ORDER BY hashtag_count DESC') USING utf8mb4), '$[*]' COLUMNS(name VARCHAR(255) PATH '$[0]', hashtag_count INT PATH '$[1]')) AS graph
sql_json: SELECT frogql_traverse('social_network_twitter', 'MATCH (h:HASHTAG)-[b:BELONGS_TO_TREND]->(tr:TREND) WHERE b.rank_position <= 5 GROUP BY tr.name RETURN tr.name, COUNT(h) AS hashtag_count ORDER BY hashtag_count DESC')

question: Retrieve the names of trends along with the number of unique hashtags associated with each trend and the average usage count of those hashtags, but only for trends promoted as content.

question: List all trends that have at least one associated hashtag used in a tweet with media attachments. For each trend, return the trend name, the number of distinct hashtags, and the total number of media attachments linked through those hashtags.

sql_json: SELECT frogql_traverse('social_network_twitter', 'MATCH (u:USER)-[:MEMBER_OF_LIST]->(l:LIST), (u)-[:POSTS]->(t:TWEET) WHERE l.is_private = false AND t.like_count > 100 GROUP BY u.username RETURN u.username, AVG(t.like_count) AS avg_likes')

question: Find users who follow at least 5 other users, have posted at least 3 tweets, and have engaged with at least 10 tweets organically. Return their usernames and the count of organic engagements.
sql: SELECT graph.username, graph.COUNTDISTINCT FROM JSON_TABLE(CONVERT(frogql_traverse('social_network_twitter', 'MATCH (u:USER)-[:FOLLOWS]->(f:USER), (u)-[:POSTS]->(t:TWEET), (u)-[e:ENGAGES_WITH]->(t:TWEET) WHERE e.is_organic = true GROUP BY u.username RETURN u.username, COUNT(DISTINCT e)') USING utf8mb4), '$[*]' COLUMNS(username VARCHAR(255) PATH '$[0]', COUNTDISTINCT INT PATH '$[1]')) AS graph
sql_json: SELECT frogql_traverse('social_network_twitter', 'MATCH (u:USER)-[:FOLLOWS]->(f:USER), (u)-[:POSTS]->(t:TWEET), (u)-[e:ENGAGES_WITH]->(t:TWEET) WHERE e.is_organic = true GROUP BY u.username RETURN u.username, COUNT(DISTINCT e)')

question: For each user who has posted at least one tweet containing a hashtag that belongs to a trend promoted as content (`promoted_content = true`), find their username and calculate how many such tweets they have posted compared to their total tweet count.
sql: SELECT graph.username, graph.COUNTDISTINCT, graph.total_tweets FROM JSON_TABLE(CONVERT(frogql_traverse('social_network_twitter', 'MATCH (u:USER)-[:POSTS]->(t:TWEET)-[:CONTAINS_HASHTAG]->(h:HASHTAG)-[:BELONGS_TO_TREND]->(tr:TREND), (u)-[:POSTS]->(any_t:TWEET) WHERE tr.promoted_content = true GROUP BY u.username RETURN u.username, COUNT(DISTINCT t), COUNT(any_t) AS total_tweets') USING utf8mb4), '$[*]' COLUMNS(username VARCHAR(255) PATH '$[0]', COUNTDISTINCT INT PATH '$[1]', total_tweets INT PATH '$[2]')) AS graph
sql_json: SELECT frogql_traverse('social_network_twitter', 'MATCH (u:USER)-[:POSTS]->(t:TWEET)-[:CONTAINS_HASHTAG]->(h:HASHTAG)-[:BELONGS_TO_TREND]->(tr:TREND), (u)-[:POSTS]->(any_t:TWEET) WHERE tr.promoted_content = true GROUP BY u.username RETURN u.username, COUNT(DISTINCT t), COUNT(any_t) AS total_tweets')

question: List the top 5 users with the highest total view counts from their tweets, who are verified and originate from a specific location. Include their display names and total view counts.
sql: SELECT graph.display_name, graph.view_count FROM JSON_TABLE(CONVERT(frogql_traverse('social_network_twitter', 'MATCH (u:USER{verified_status:true})-[:POSTS]->(t:TWEET)-[:ORIGINATES_FROM]->(:LOCATION) GROUP BY u.display_name RETURN u.display_name, SUM(t.view_count) ORDER BY SUM(t.view_count) DESC LIMIT 5') USING utf8mb4), '$[*]' COLUMNS(display_name VARCHAR(255) PATH '$[0]', view_count INT PATH '$[1]')) AS graph

question: Retrieve the display names of users who have engaged with tweets containing media attachments and have also followed at least 5 other users. Include the total number of media attachments in the tweets they engaged with.

sql_json: SELECT frogql_traverse('social_network_twitter', 'MATCH (u:USER)-[:ENGAGES_WITH]->(t:TWEET)-[:ATTACHES_MEDIA]->(m:MEDIA_ATTACHMENT), (u)-[f:FOLLOWS]->(:USER) GROUP BY u.display_name RETURN u.display_name, COUNT(DISTINCT m)')

question: Retrieve the average view count of tweets that contain media attachments and were posted by verified users. Group the results by media type and order them by average view count in descending order.
sql: SELECT graph.media_type, graph.avg_view_count FROM JSON_TABLE(CONVERT(frogql_traverse('social_network_twitter', 'MATCH (u:USER {verified_status: true})-[:POSTS]->(t:TWEET)-[:ATTACHES_MEDIA]->(m:MEDIA_ATTACHMENT) GROUP BY m.media_type RETURN m.media_type, AVG(t.view_count) AS avg_view_count ORDER BY avg_view_count DESC') USING utf8mb4), '$[*]' COLUMNS(media_type VARCHAR(255) PATH '$[0]', avg_view_count DOUBLE PATH '$[1]')) AS graph
sql_json: SELECT frogql_traverse('social_network_twitter', 'MATCH (u:USER {verified_status: true})-[:POSTS]->(t:TWEET)-[:ATTACHES_MEDIA]->(m:MEDIA_ATTACHMENT) GROUP BY m.media_type RETURN m.media_type, AVG(t.view_count) AS avg_view_count ORDER BY avg_view_count DESC')

question: Identify users who have posted tweets in more than one language and have also engaged with tweets in at least three different languages. Return their usernames and the count of distinct languages in which they have engaged.
sql: SELECT graph.username, graph.COUNTDISTINCT FROM JSON_TABLE(CONVERT(frogql_traverse('social_network_twitter', 'MATCH (u:USER)-[:POSTS]->(t:TWEET), (u)-[e:ENGAGES_WITH]->(t_eng:TWEET) GROUP BY u.username RETURN u.username, COUNT(DISTINCT t_eng.language)') USING utf8mb4), '$[*]' COLUMNS(username VARCHAR(255) PATH '$[0]', COUNTDISTINCT INT PATH '$[1]')) AS graph
sql_json: SELECT frogql_traverse('social_network_twitter', 'MATCH (u:USER)-[:POSTS]->(t:TWEET), (u)-[e:ENGAGES_WITH]->(t_eng:TWEET) GROUP BY u.username RETURN u.username, COUNT(DISTINCT t_eng.language)')

question: Identify users who follow at least 5 other users and have posted tweets that originated from more than 2 distinct locations. Return their usernames and the number of distinct locations their tweets originated from.
sql: SELECT graph.username, graph.COUNTDISTINCT FROM JSON_TABLE(CONVERT(frogql_traverse('social_network_twitter', 'MATCH (u:USER)-[:FOLLOWS]->(f:USER), (u)-[:POSTS]->(t:TWEET)-[:ORIGINATES_FROM]->(l:LOCATION) GROUP BY u.username RETURN u.username, COUNT(DISTINCT l.location_id)') USING utf8mb4), '$[*]' COLUMNS(username VARCHAR(255) PATH '$[0]', COUNTDISTINCT INT PATH '$[1]')) AS graph

question: List the users who have posted tweets containing hashtags belonging to trends promoted as content and have also engaged with at least one of those tweets. Return their usernames and the count of such engagements.
sql: SELECT graph.username, graph.engagement_count FROM JSON_TABLE(CONVERT(frogql_traverse('social_network_twitter', 'MATCH (u:USER)-[:POSTS]->(t:TWEET)-[:CONTAINS_HASHTAG]->(h:HASHTAG)-[:BELONGS_TO_TREND]->(tr:TREND), (u)-[e:ENGAGES_WITH]->(t) WHERE tr.promoted_content = true GROUP BY u.username RETURN u.username, COUNT(e) AS engagement_count') USING utf8mb4), '$[*]' COLUMNS(username VARCHAR(255) PATH '$[0]', engagement_count INT PATH '$[1]')) AS graph

question: Identify users who have posted tweets with media attachments and have also engaged organically with at least one tweet containing a hashtag belonging to a trend with a tweet volume greater than 10000. Return their usernames and the total count of distinct media attachments they've posted.
sql: SELECT graph.username, graph.COUNTDISTINCT FROM JSON_TABLE(CONVERT(frogql_traverse('social_network_twitter', 'MATCH (u:USER)-[:POSTS]->(t1:TWEET)-[:ATTACHES_MEDIA]->(m:MEDIA_ATTACHMENT), (u)-[:ENGAGES_WITH{is_organic:true}]->(t2:TWEET)-[:CONTAINS_HASHTAG]->(h:HASHTAG)-[:BELONGS_TO_TREND]->(tr:TREND) WHERE tr.tweet_volume > 10000 GROUP BY u.username RETURN u.username, COUNT(DISTINCT m)') USING utf8mb4), '$[*]' COLUMNS(username VARCHAR(255) PATH '$[0]', COUNTDISTINCT INT PATH '$[1]')) AS graph
sql_json: SELECT frogql_traverse('social_network_twitter', 'MATCH (u:USER)-[:POSTS]->(t1:TWEET)-[:ATTACHES_MEDIA]->(m:MEDIA_ATTACHMENT), (u)-[:ENGAGES_WITH{is_organic:true}]->(t2:TWEET)-[:CONTAINS_HASHTAG]->(h:HASHTAG)-[:BELONGS_TO_TREND]->(tr:TREND) WHERE tr.tweet_volume > 10000 GROUP BY u.username RETURN u.username, COUNT(DISTINCT m)')

question: Find the top 5 locations with the highest number of geo-tagged tweets that are in a language other than English and contain at least one hashtag. For each location, return its name and the count of such tweets.
sql: SELECT graph.name, graph.COUNTDISTINCT FROM JSON_TABLE(CONVERT(frogql_traverse('social_network_twitter', 'MATCH (l:LOCATION)<-[:ORIGINATES_FROM]-(t:TWEET)-[:CONTAINS_HASHTAG]->(:HASHTAG) WHERE t.language <> ''en'' GROUP BY l.name RETURN l.name, COUNT(DISTINCT t) ORDER BY COUNT(DISTINCT t) DESC LIMIT 5') USING utf8mb4), '$[*]' COLUMNS(name VARCHAR(255) PATH '$[0]', COUNTDISTINCT INT PATH '$[1]')) AS graph
sql_json: SELECT frogql_traverse('social_network_twitter', 'MATCH (l:LOCATION)<-[:ORIGINATES_FROM]-(t:TWEET)-[:CONTAINS_HASHTAG]->(:HASHTAG) WHERE t.language <> ''en'' GROUP BY l.name RETURN l.name, COUNT(DISTINCT t) ORDER BY COUNT(DISTINCT t) DESC LIMIT 5')

question: Determine the average number of followers for users who have posted tweets in Spanish (language code 'es') and have at least one media attachment. Also, ensure that these tweets have been viewed more than 100 times. Return the calculated average follower count.

question: Determine the average number of tweets posted per user for users who have posted at least one tweet with sensitive content and have a verified status. Also, return the maximum view count among their tweets.

question: Identify the top 5 users who have the highest total engagement (sum of likes, retweets, and replies) across all their tweets, considering only tweets that contain media attachments. Return their display names and total engagement scores.

sql: SELECT graph.user_id, graph.bio FROM JSON_TABLE(CONVERT(frogql_traverse('social_network_twitter', 'MATCH (n:USER) WHERE n.bio IS NOT NULL RETURN n.user_id, n.bio') USING utf8mb4), '$[*]' COLUMNS(user_id INT PATH '$[0]', bio VARCHAR(255) PATH '$[1]')) AS graph

question: Find users whose followers_count is greater than 100. Return their user_id and followers_count.

question: Find entities reachable within 1 to 3 hops from the user 'Tiffany Johnson' via any relationship, returning their IDs and names (if available), limited to 5 results.
sql: SELECT graph.id, graph.name FROM JSON_TABLE(CONVERT(frogql_traverse('social_network_twitter', 'MATCH (n1:USER)-[]->{1,3}(n2) WHERE n1.display_name = ''Tiffany Johnson'' RETURN n2.id, n2.name LIMIT 5') USING utf8mb4), '$[*]' COLUMNS(id INT PATH '$[0]', name VARCHAR(255) PATH '$[1]')) AS graph
sql_json: SELECT frogql_traverse('social_network_twitter', 'MATCH (n1:USER)-[]->{1,3}(n2) WHERE n1.display_name = ''Tiffany Johnson'' RETURN n2.id, n2.name LIMIT 5')

question: List the display name of the user and the ID of tweets they posted, limited to 20 results.
sql: SELECT graph.display_name, graph.id FROM JSON_TABLE(CONVERT(frogql_traverse('social_network_twitter', 'MATCH (a:USER)-[r:POSTS]->(b) RETURN a.display_name, b.id LIMIT 20') USING utf8mb4), '$[*]' COLUMNS(display_name VARCHAR(255) PATH '$[0]', id INT PATH '$[1]')) AS graph
sql_json: SELECT frogql_traverse('social_network_twitter', 'MATCH (a:USER)-[r:POSTS]->(b) RETURN a.display_name, b.id LIMIT 20')

sql_json: SELECT frogql_traverse('social_network_twitter', 'MATCH (n1:USER)-[:POSTS]->{1,3}(n2) WHERE n1.user_id = ''U000001'' RETURN n2.id, n2.name LIMIT 5')

question: Find paths up to 4 hops long between users and tweets using POSTS or other relevant edges, returning user and tweet IDs.

question: Retrieve the display name and bio of the user with username 'robert00'.
sql: SELECT graph.display_name, graph.bio FROM JSON_TABLE(CONVERT(frogql_traverse('social_network_twitter', 'MATCH (n:USER) WHERE n.username = ''robert00'' RETURN n.display_name, n.bio LIMIT 10') USING utf8mb4), '$[*]' COLUMNS(display_name VARCHAR(255) PATH '$[0]', bio VARCHAR(255) PATH '$[1]')) AS graph

question: Find tweets posted by the user 'Tiffany Johnson' and return her display name along with the tweet IDs.
sql: SELECT graph.display_name, graph.tweet_id FROM JSON_TABLE(CONVERT(frogql_traverse('social_network_twitter', 'MATCH (a:USER)-[r:POSTS]->(b:TWEET) WHERE a.display_name = ''Tiffany Johnson'' RETURN a.display_name, b.tweet_id LIMIT 20') USING utf8mb4), '$[*]' COLUMNS(display_name VARCHAR(255) PATH '$[0]', tweet_id INT PATH '$[1]')) AS graph
sql_json: SELECT frogql_traverse('social_network_twitter', 'MATCH (a:USER)-[r:POSTS]->(b:TWEET) WHERE a.display_name = ''Tiffany Johnson'' RETURN a.display_name, b.tweet_id LIMIT 20')

question: Retrieve the display name of users who posted tweets and the corresponding tweet text for those posts.
sql: SELECT graph.display_name, graph.text FROM JSON_TABLE(CONVERT(frogql_traverse('social_network_twitter', 'MATCH (a:USER)-[r:POSTS]->(b:TWEET) RETURN a.display_name, b.text LIMIT 20') USING utf8mb4), '$[*]' COLUMNS(display_name VARCHAR(255) PATH '$[0]', text TEXT PATH '$[1]')) AS graph
sql_json: SELECT frogql_traverse('social_network_twitter', 'MATCH (a:USER)-[r:POSTS]->(b:TWEET) RETURN a.display_name, b.text LIMIT 20')
